repo_analysis_summary: LineIndex.build on improve/lineindex_build_throughput (1d2377e, src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L232-375) now has the round-2 string-skip loop (L256-282: escaped carry, 4x-unrolled 'buf[i..i+3] > 0x5c' reject, byte tail) plus the round-3 WCLS outer skip (L301-305: table-driven non-structural byte runs). Sealed score 1.623 vs target 1.8 (gap 0.177). Round-3 brief measured swarU32 (aligned Uint32Array SWAR string scanner) stacked on skipCls at ~1.21x relative to the round-2 baseline (sealed ~1.80-1.85), but H001 requires single-change plans so round 3 landed skipCls first. Round-4 scratch harness (outside the repo, /tmp/li-exp: g5.mjs generator + g5run.mjs runner + sweep6/7.sh): each candidate is one change on top of the current merged code (rej4+skipCls), tested via differential check on sealed edge fixtures (whole/1/2/7/64/1000-byte splits, intervals 1024/1/3, async-iterable and string chunks) then 31 paired runs vs the reference in the same Node v24.21 process (alternating order, median ratio). Because absolute throughput drifts with thermal/ESET load (mirror ranged 1.45-1.67 across processes), results are reported as 'relative' = candidate ratio / mirror ratio in the same pass. Method: sweep6 (passes 1-2, 7 candidates each) then sweep7 (passes 3-4, top 5 candidates). Results: swarU32 1.144/1.113/1.116/1.168 (median ~1.13x relative, sealed ~1.83); rej4u32 1.077/1.080/1.060/1.114 (median ~1.08x, sealed ~1.75); viewU8, skipDef, quoteDirect, rej4n3 all within noise (1.01-1.05x, inconsistent). swarU32+viewU8 stack 1.114/1.138 = no gain over swarU32 alone, confirming viewU8 is neutral. The round-3 brief's swarU32 stack prediction (~1.80-1.85) is confirmed by this measurement (~1.83 sealed).

ideas.title: Aligned Uint32Array SWAR string skip (swarU32): replace the 4x byte reject with a word loop testing for 0x22/0x5c via haszero
ideas.source: Scratch g5.mjs candidate 'A swarU32'; sweep6.log passes 1-2, sweep7.log passes 3-4; round-3 brief idea 2 (measured stacked, now measured alone on merged code)
ideas.evidence: Relative to the mirror baseline in the same pass: 1.144 (pass 1: 1.750/1.489 vs mirror 1.508/1.468), 1.113 (pass 2: 1.654/1.439 vs 1.565/1.517), 1.116 (pass 3: 1.664/1.464 vs 1.483/1.455), 1.168 (pass 4: 1.906/1.608 vs 1.672/1.648); median ~1.13x. Expected sealed score 1.623 × 1.13 ≈ 1.83, matching round-3 brief's stack prediction. Single change, string branch only. Per chunk: const base = buf.byteOffset; const aOff = (base + 3) & ~3; const wN = base + n > aOff ? (base + n - aOff) >> 2 : 0; const u32 = new Uint32Array(buf.buffer, aOff, wN); In the string loop, replace the 4x unrolled while with: if (((base + i) & 3) === 0) { let w = (base + i - aOff) >> 2; while (w < wN) { const x = u32[w]; const a = x ^ 0x22222222, c = x ^ 0x5c5c5c5c; if (((((a - 0x01010101) & ~a) | ((c - 0x01010101) & ~c)) & 0x80808080) !== 0) break; w++; } i = aOff - base + (w << 2); } and keep the existing byte tail. The byte tail walks to the next aligned word on its own, so unaligned subarrays, pooled Buffer.from(string) buffers and 1-byte splits pass; haszero is byte-wise so endianness does not matter, and a false positive only drops to the byte path. Correctness confirmed on all sealed edge fixtures plus extras (trailing backslash at EOF, escaped-quote runs, unicode/emoji, leading empty lines, raw newlines inside strings), splits whole/1/2/7/64/1000 bytes, intervals 1024/1/3, async-iterable input and string chunks. Outer skip, checkpoint logic, record pushes and for-await loop stay untouched. This is the change expected to cross 1.8.

ideas.title: Word-wise 4x reject on the aligned Uint32Array (rej4u32): same structure as idea 1 but test each byte lane > 0x5c instead of haszero
ideas.source: Scratch g5.mjs candidate 'B rej4u32'; sweep6.log passes 1-2, sweep7.log passes 3-4; round-3 brief idea 3 (measured stacked, now measured alone)
ideas.evidence: Relative: 1.077 (pass 1: 1.590/1.437 vs 1.508/1.468), 1.080 (pass 2: 1.755/1.574 vs 1.565/1.517), 1.060 (pass 3: 1.749/1.620 vs 1.483/1.455), 1.114 (pass 4: 1.825/1.614 vs 1.672/1.648); median ~1.08x. Expected sealed ~1.75. Same per-chunk u32 setup and alignment guard as idea 1; the word test is: if (((x & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 8 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 16 & 0xff) <= 0x5c) || ((x >>> 24) <= 0x5c)) break; It keeps the merged code's '> 0x5c' semantics (stops on any byte <= 0x5c, not just quote/backslash), so the existing byte tail is unchanged. Same family and same hypothesis slot as idea 1: plan one or the other, not both. Pick this one if the planner wants the smaller, more predictable delta (lower variance across passes: 1.06-1.11 vs swarU32's 1.11-1.17); pick idea 1 for the higher sealed estimate (1.83 vs 1.75). Round-3 brief listed this as slightly below swarU32 when stacked (1.19-1.21x vs 1.21-1.24x); measurements here confirm the same ranking when measured alone.

ideas.title: NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE: Uint8Array view (viewU8), default-case skip (skipDef), quote-direct handling (quoteDirect), n-3 hoist (rej4n3)
ideas.source: Scratch g5.mjs candidates 'C skipDef', 'D quoteDirect', 'E rej4n3', 'F viewU8'; sweep6.log passes 1-2, sweep7.log passes 3-4
ideas.evidence: viewU8 (const buf = new Uint8Array(src0.buffer, src0.byteOffset, src0.length) instead of Buffer): 1.050 (pass 1), 1.094 (pass 2), 1.013 (pass 3), 1.020 (pass 4); noisy, likely neutral since Buffer and Uint8Array share the same V8 element kind. skipDef (move the WCLS content-run skip into the switch default branch instead of a pre-check before the switch, saving one table lookup per structural byte): 1.034 (pass 1), 1.076 (pass 2); inconsistent, structural bytes are a small fraction of total. quoteDirect (case 0x22: inString = true; lineHasContent = true; i++; continue; to skip the trailing i++ and outer re-check): 1.050 (pass 1), 1.041 (pass 2); within noise, the continue path still pays an outer-loop branch and the savings are under 1%. rej4n3 (hoist n-3 as const n3 = n - 3 and change the string-loop unroll guard to i < n3 instead of i + 3 < n): 1.031 (pass 1), 1.070 (pass 2); within noise, the extra local vs the in-loop add is compiler-optimized. None worth planning; listed so planners do not resubmit them. swarU32+viewU8 stack (passes 3-4 only): 1.114, 1.138 vs swarU32 alone 1.116, 1.168, confirming viewU8 adds nothing when combined.

ideas.title: STILL REJECTED from rounds 1-3: chunk-iteration reshaping, lazy/typed record storage, Buffer#indexOf skipping, table lookup inside strings, nextCp counter, quote-check before the switch
ideas.source: iteration_history round_1.json, round_2.json, round_3.json; research_briefs round_2.json and round_3.json
ideas.evidence: Sync scanChunk kernel 0.897 (round 1) and index-based array loop 0.882 (round 2): no effect, ~16 chunks per build. Lazy recordEndLines 5-10% slower, Float64Array record offsets 15-20% slower (round 2). Buffer#indexOf quote/newline skipping slower on short strings and wrong for raw newlines inside strings (round 2). Uint8Array class table inside strings slower than the plain '> 0x5c' compare (round 2). nextCp (counter instead of line % interval) neutral across rounds 1-3 (1.002, 0.993 in round 3). quoteFirst (peel 0x22 case before the switch) neutral or negative (0.999, 0.973 in round 3). Not re-measured this round; listed so planners do not resubmit them.
